title: Write the candidate list: forcing moves, one quiet move, a reason each
outcomes: Writes two to four candidates with forcing moves first, one quiet move, and a one-line purpose for each
Drops a candidate only by naming the reply that refutes it
Spots a list with no quiet move, or one that repeats one piece along one line
Recognises a position with one legal move, where there is nothing to list

steps.text: **Write the list, with a reason for each.** The short list in your head becomes a paper list: two to four moves, **checks and captures first**, then **at least one quiet move** (no check, no capture). Beside each, one line: *what does it do?* A move comes off only when you can name the reply that refutes it. 'It looks bad' is not a reason.

steps.caption: White to move. A written list. A) Rf8+ : check on the eighth rank. B) Rxg7+ : check, taking the g7 pawn. C) Rcc7 : quiet; the second rook joins the first on the seventh rank. A comes off: after ...Rxf8 White is at least three points down. B comes off: after ...Kxg7 White is at least two points down. C stays.

line.say: Rcc7 gives no check and takes nothing. Both rooks now stand on the seventh rank.
Ra1+ is a check of its own: quiet moves can meet a forcing reply.
Kf2 steps out of the check. Rcc7 is still the engine's best move (depth 16).

claims.statement: Rcc7 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
After Rcc7 a white rook stands on c7.
After Rcc7 the other white rook still stands on f7.
Rf8+ is at least 10 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
After Rf8+ and Black's best defence White is at least 3 points down.
After Rf8+ Rxf8 a black rook stands on f8: the reply is legal and takes the rook.
After Rxg7+ Kxg7 the black king stands on g7: the king takes the rook.
Rxg7+ is at least 10 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
Rf8+ attacks the king on g8: it is check.
Rxg7+ takes a pawn: a black pawn stands on g7.
Rxg7 is check: the rook on g7 attacks g8.
After Rcc7, Ra1+ is check: the rook on a1 attacks g1.
The king can step to f2.
After Rxg7+ and Black's best defence White is at least 2 points down.

steps.text: **When the list helps, and when it fails.** It helps when more than one plan is plausible. It fails three ways. Near-duplicates: three moves of one rook along one rank look at one piece and no other. A move dropped by feel: name the reply or keep it. A position with one legal move, where there is nothing to list. 'Forcing first, one quiet' is a rule of thumb.

steps.title: Same forcing candidate, one pawn moved
steps.prompt: In the first position a white pawn stands on c2. In the second it stands on c3; everything else is the same. In each, write your list and find the best move. Predict first: does the forcing candidate still work?

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Each exercise has three hints. The next three are silent: no hints and no engine line before you answer. If you play another move, the app may still check it with the engine afterwards. Write your list on paper before you move. Hints only on request, once you solve unlabeled items without them, is planned, not built yet.

steps.prompt: Look at your paper lists for the silent positions. Count honestly. This note stays on this device.

steps.text: **Next: two more exercises.** Most are puzzles from the general bank where you enter a whole line: your move, the reply, your next move. They test calculation more than listing, so write your list first and name the reply that refutes each forcing move you drop.

**List sheet: ten minutes, away from the app.** Take ten positions from your own games where you had to choose; the biggest drops under My games are a good source. Cover the move you played. For each, write two to four candidates (never more) with a one-line purpose: forcing moves first, one quiet. Uncover. A hit means the best move was on your list. Hits out of ten: your baseline.
